To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. PDE5 inhibitors have cognition enhancing effects in standard laboratory conditions, 2. PDE5 inhibition has no cognition enhancing effects in animals housed under enriched environment conditions, 3. The cognition enhancing effects of PDE5 inhibition in standard conditions are not related to changes in CREB signaling, and 4. The cognition enhancing effect of PDE5 inhibitors in standard conditions may be related to the activation of the MAPK signaling pathway.
PDE5 inhibitors only improve object memory in rats housed in a socially standardized environment, but not in rats housed in an EE, which is assumed to be more similar to the human environment.

(1) EE animals had a better object memory performance than animals housed under standard conditions; (2) PDE5 inhibition did not affect object memory performance in EE animals; (3) PDE5 mRNA expression levels were comparable between experimental groups, whereas pCREB levels and the number of synapses were higher in EE animals; and (4) these data suggest that PDE5 inhibition might be a valid target to improve cognition in patients with memory impairment, but not in patients with normal

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PDE5 inhibition improves memory performance under standard housing conditions but not under EE conditions.

the use of EE rats is a more valid model to study memory enhancing drugs, as the effects of PDE5 inhibitors on memory are similar to those in humans, but that the use of SOC or SOL rats is a more appropriate model to study the memory impairing effects of drugs.
the use of an EE housing paradigm may provide a better model of human memory performance and thus may help in the development of new cognition enhancing drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of drugs in the rat ORT are not necessarily generalizable to humans, as the effects of PDE5 inhibition on object memory in the rat OR task depend on the housing conditions of the rats.
PDE5 inhibition is not a promising approach for the treatment of human memory impairments.
PDE5 inhibition improves memory in standard housed rats but not in EE rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EE animals may be more suitable to study memory effects of drugs in the rat ORT.
EE housing is not only a more valid model of memory, but also of PDE5 inhibition.
EE rats may not be suitable for testing cognition enhancing compounds, as the effects of EE on the brain may already optimize the signaling pathways that the drug targets.
